explain.say: Female sea turtles return to the beach where they themselves hatched, often decades later, to lay their eggs. It is one of the most remarkable homing journeys in nature.

explain.say: At night the female crawls up the beach, digs a deep hole with her back flippers and lays around 100 soft, leathery eggs. She covers them with sand and returns to the sea, never seeing her young.

explain.say: The warmth of the sand decides whether each baby becomes male or female. Cooler nests produce mostly males and warmer nests mostly females, balancing near 29 degrees Celsius, so warming beaches are a worry.

After about two months the hatchlings dig out together, usually at night, and race for the brightest horizon, which on a natural beach is the open sea. Bright lights from buildings can lure them the wrong way.

faq.q: How do sea turtles find the beach where they hatched?
faq.a: Scientists think hatchlings memorise the magnetic signature of their home beach, its particular strength and angle of Earth's magnetic field. Years later, adult females follow the field back to the coastline that matches.
asks: How do turtles navigate the ocean?
Do turtles return to the same beach?

faq.q: Does sand temperature decide if turtles are male or female?
faq.a: Yes. In sea turtles the temperature of the nest during the middle of incubation sets the sex. Warmer nests produce mostly females, cooler ones mostly males, with an even mix near 29 degrees Celsius.
asks: Why are most baby turtles female?
How does heat change turtle eggs?

faq.q: How do hatchlings find the sea?
faq.a: Hatchlings head for the lowest, brightest horizon, which on a dark natural beach is the sea reflecting the sky. Once in the water, they swim into the waves and later use the magnetic field to steer.
asks: How do baby turtles know where the ocean is?
Why do turtles crawl towards lights?

faq.a: Very few. Crabs, birds and fish eat many hatchlings, and an often-quoted estimate is that only about one in a thousand lives to become an adult.
asks: Why do so few baby turtles survive?

faq.a: After reaching the sea, young turtles drift for years in ocean currents, often sheltering in floating seaweed, before settling at coastal feeding grounds. They were hard to track, so this time was called the lost years.
asks: What do young sea turtles do?

facts: In many sea turtles, nests at about 29 °C produce roughly equal numbers of males and females.
Loggerhead turtles appear to nest where the beach's magnetic signature matches the one they knew as hatchlings (Brothers and Lohmann, 2015).
